title: Customer peer networking failover & RTT requirements (edge-to-control)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:

This document defines minimal and recommended peer-networking and failover requirements for Redwood private deployments (VPC-connected and on-prem edge sites) with a focus on round-trip time (RTT), failover behavior, and measurable telemetry needed for acceptance and ongoing SLA compliance. It is intended for operators, field engineers, and customer networking teams responsible for connecting customer networks to Redwood control planes and runtime endpoints.

Scope and audience:

- Scope: connectivity between customer tenant endpoints (edge or on-prem runtime) and Redwood control plane / model-serving endpoints used for model routing, telemetry ingestion, and control messages.
- Audience: field ops, SRE, onboarding engineers, customer network architects, solutions engineers.

Goals:

1. Provide deterministic thresholds for RTT, jitter, and packet loss for different workload classes (latency-sensitive, throughput-oriented, telemetry).
2. Define failover behavior and expected time-to-recover (TTR) for common failure modes (link, BGP flap, VPN tunnel outage, regional control-plane failover).
3. Specify test and acceptance procedures (commands, expected outputs) used during onboarding and periodic validation.
4. List telemetry signals and alerting thresholds needed by Redwood to detect customer-visible regressions.

Definitions and workload classes:

- Latency-sensitive: interactive chat/assistant inference where tail token latency impacts UX. Typical traffic: small requests, streaming responses.
- Throughput-oriented: batch embeddings / reranking jobs tolerant of higher per-request latency but sensitive to sustained bandwidth.
- Control/telemetry: heartbeat, KV state replication, health-check streams; low bandwidth but strict delivery expectations for correctness.

Minimal baseline network requirements (acceptance):

| Metric                   | Latency-sensitive SLA | Throughput SLA       | Notes |
|-------------------------|-----------------------|----------------------|-------|
| RTT (p95)               | <= 45 ms              | <= 150 ms            | Measured edge -> control-plane region; p99 targets in notes. |
| Packet loss (1m avg)    | < 0.5%                | < 1.0%               | Loss above triggers immediate investigation. |
| Inter-packet jitter (p95)| < 8 ms               | < 20 ms              | Burst jitter tolerated for short windows. |
| Bandwidth (sustained)   | 50 Mbps per 1000 concurrent users | 1 Gbps for heavy batch nodes | Size to be adjusted by customer scale. |
| MTU                     | >= 1400 bytes         | >= 1400 bytes        | Path MTU discovery must succeed. |
| Symmetric NAT           | Unsupported for certain control-plane auth modes | See VPN note | Use NAT traversal only for non-privileged setups. |
| BGP/Route convergence   | < 60 seconds (planned maintenance) | < 120 seconds | Route flaps degrade token streaming; limits enforced. |

Recommended / aspirational targets (for premium customers):

- RTT p99 <= 80 ms for latency-sensitive workloads.
- Packet loss (5m moving average) < 0.2%.
- Jitter p99 < 12 ms.
- Redundant control-plane paths with < 3s failover for TCP-based streaming (when using dedicated interconnect + BFD).

Failover modes and expected behavior:

1) VPN tunnel outage (customer-managed IPSec):
   - Expected detection: Redwood control plane sees TCP connection reset and missing keepalives within 30s.
   - Customer expectation: re-establish or switch to backup tunnel within 60s for degraded but functional service; full restore within 180s.
   - Operator steps: (a) Verify tunnels via "show crypto ipsec sa" (vendor CLI) or equivalent; (b) verify BGP adjacency; (c) switch traffic via secondary route if primary fails.

2) BGP route flap or next-hop loss:
   - Expected detection: control-plane routing table changes observed; traffic shifts to secondary path. Redwood tolerates transient flaps < 30s.
   - TTR expectation: under normal config with BFD enabled, < 3s; without BFD, < 60s.

3) Regional control-plane failover (Redwood side):
   - Behavior: automatic routing to next-closest verified region/model variant. Customers should expect temporary increases in RTT consistent with regional hop differences and potential model variant fallbacks as per agreement.
   - Communication: automatic incident note + email and console banner.

Acceptance test checklist (onboarding):

1. Baseline measurements (edge host placed in scheduled test harness):
   - Run: ping -i 0.2 -c 100 <control-plane-ip> and record p50/p95/p99.
   - Run: iperf3 -c <control-plane> -t 60 -P 10 to validate sustained throughput.
   - Run: mtr -z --report <control-plane> for 120 probes to capture hop jitter patterns.

2. Packet loss simulation: use tc/netem on edge host to inject 1% loss for 60s and verify degraded connection detection and failover. Expected: control plane flags loss and opens fallback route.

3. BGP failover exercise: withdraw primary route from customer router; measure convergence and route re-announce time. Expected: BFD-enabled convergence < 3s; otherwise < 60s.

4. VPN failover test: bring down primary tunnel and validate traffic flow through secondary. Expected: application-level streaming resumes within 60-180s depending on tunnel ramp.

Operator runbook (quick steps):

1. Verify reachability:
   - ping -c 10 <control-plane>
   - tcpdump -i <iface> host <control-plane> and verify SYN/ACK flows
2. Check BGP state:
   - show ip bgp summary | grep <peer>
3. Check tunnel state (IPSec example):
   - show crypto isakmp sa
   - show crypto ipsec sa | include <peer-ip>
4. If failover not automatic: manually update route to point to backup next-hop and notify Redwood success channel.

Config example (YAML config fragment used by field agent to declare network requirements to Redwood):

---
agent_network_profile:
  name: "customer-edge-nyc-01"
  expected_rtt_ms_p95: 45
  expected_packet_loss_pct: 0.5
  preferred_transport: "ipsec" # alternatives: "bgp-direct", "aws-interconnect"
  bfd_enabled: true
  mtu: 1500
  redundancy:
    vpn_peers: ["10.10.0.1","10.10.0.2"]
    bgp_primary: "10.0.0.1"
---

(This fragment is used by the onboarding operator to generate the expected acceptance checks and to configure telemetry collection fields on Redwood side.)

Telemetry signals and alerting thresholds (what Redwood needs from customer or must be observable):

- RTT histogram (1s buckets) edge -> control-plane; alert if p95 > configured threshold for 5m.
- Packet loss percentage per 1m; alert if > configured threshold for 3m.
- TCP retransmits and zero-window events; alert if spikes > baseline by 3x for 2m.
- BGP adjacency flaps and number of route withdrawals; alert if > 3 withdraws in 10 minutes.
- Tunnel uptime percentage (daily); alert if < 99.5% for production-class tenants.

Acceptance gate PvRs (pre-deployment acceptance):

- Gate A (connectivity baseline): All baseline tests pass and agent_network_profile fields are populated.
- Gate B (failover validation): VPN and BGP failover scenarios executed and documented in on-call runbook.
- Gate C (telemetry): Continuous telemetry stream validated for 24 hours with no critical alerts.

Escalation and rollback guidance:

- If a failover test causes application regressions that cannot be mitigated via route failover, rollback to staged maintenance window: disable new routes and revert to known-good topology.
- Communication templates (short):
  - Subject: [ACTION REQUIRED] Network failover caused degraded inference latency for tenant <TENANT>.
  - Body: Summary of timeline, measured p95/p99 before and after, current mitigation, next steps.

Ownership and contacts:

- Onboarding owner: Field Onboarding Team (owner: Diego Morales)
- Network escalation: SRE-Networking (oncall)
- Customer contact: Solutions Engineer assigned during onboarding

Appendix A — Measurements & sample command outputs:

- Sample ping output snippet (p95 ~ 32ms):

--- 34.120.10.8 ping statistics ---
100 packets transmitted, 100 received, 0% packet loss, time 99123ms
rtt min/avg/max/mdev = 31.569/33.102/45.786/2.311 ms

- Sample iperf3:

[SUM]   0.00-60.00 sec  1.02 GBytes   146 Mbits/sec  sender

Appendix B — Frequently encountered pitfalls and mitigations:

- Asymmetric routing: Causes failed TLS handshakes and unexpected packet loss. Mitigate by ensuring symmetric routing for control-plane subnets or by enabling TCP MTU blackhole detection and path MTU discovery.
- Deep packet inspection (DPI) appliances: May drop long-lived TLS streams; recommend bypass or apply permissive policies for control-plane IPs.
- Misconfigured NAT timeouts: Long-lived streaming sessions may be reset; set NAT keepalive intervals < 60s or use BFD and TCP keepalives.
